page: Vultr voc-m-4c-32gb-400s-amd is an AMD-based instance within the Optimized Cloud Compute family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical AMD EPYC cores running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per core ratio. Storage is provided via a local 400 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present on this configuration.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance ranking in the top tier. Single-threaded tasks such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also show strong performance in the top 25%. However, multi-threaded scaling presents some limitations; multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and passmark database operations fall into the bottom 25%. Memory performance is robust, with the passmark memory score and large-block write bandwidth both placing in the top 25%, while read bandwidth remains average.

Given the 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and the 400 GB NVMe SSD, this instance is well-suited for memory-intensive workloads, caching layers, and moderate storage-bound applications. However, the lower multi-threaded decompression and database operation benchmarks suggest it may face bottlenecks under highly concurrent database writes or heavy multi-threaded processing. It is highly capable for single-threaded execution, memory-bound computations, and general-purpose workloads requiring a larger memory footprint relative to compute cores.
